age.evidence: All rats were in an advanced adult age >PND180, with animals in the control group ranging between 6-12 months and the experimental group being 14 months at the recording time.

sex.evidence: We used male Wistar rats from the breeding colony at the CIMH.

dosing.evidence: On days 6 and 9 after initial recordings, alcohol-dependent rats randomly received intraperitoneal (i.p.) injections of psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg ... dissolved in Ampuwa ... each 30 min before recording.
LY379268 (1 mg/kg, 1R,4R,5S,6R)-4-Amino-2-oxabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-4,6-dicarboxylic acid, Tocris Bioscience) each 30 min before recording.

handling.evidence: Methods describe two weeks of habituation to the animal room but do not describe a specific handling protocol.

group_housing.evidence: Rats were housed in single cages (Makrolon ®, Type III, Tecniplast Deutschland GmbH).

day_night_flipped.evidence: Housing rooms were temperature (20 - 22°C) and humidity (40 - 55%) controlled with a 12 h automatic light-dark cycle (lights on at 6.00 am).

enrichment_housing.evidence: Rats were housed ... on sawdust bedding (Ssniff - Bedding 3/4 S, Altrogge) with Bed-r' Nest material (Datesand Ltd.).

assays.assay_name: Long-term voluntary alcohol consumption with repeated deprivation (Alcohol Deprivation Effect)
assays.assay_description: Home-cage four-bottle voluntary drinking paradigm with concurrent access to water and 5%, 10% and 20% ethanol solutions, repeatedly interrupted by 2-3 week deprivation phases over more than a year. Daily ethanol intake (g/kg) was measured at baseline (last week of a drinking phase) and on the first day after deprivation to quantify the alcohol deprivation effect (ADE). Psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg i.p.) and LY379268 (1 mg/kg i.p.) effects on the ADE are referenced from prior work.

application_type.evidence: alcohol-dependent rats randomly received intraperitoneal (i.p.) injections of psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg) ... or LY379268 (1 mg/kg) ... each 30 min before recording.

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were habituated to the animal room but the paper does not describe a separate habituation to the drinking apparatus beyond the long initial drinking phase.

setup_restrain.evidence: Drinking occurred freely in the home cage from bottles with special spillage-minimizing caps.

food_restriction.evidence: Pelleted food (V1534-300, ssniff Spezialdiäten GmbH) and water were available ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: Water was available ad libitum alongside the ethanol bottles throughout.

time_to_assay.evidence: Baseline intake measured during the last week of drinking phases and ADE measured on the first day after 2-3 week deprivation periods, across multiple cycles over >1 year.

sample_size.evidence: rats (n = 10) were given ad libitum access to ethanol ... solutions of 5%, 10%, and 20%.

outcomes.summary: Following each deprivation period, rats showed a pronounced alcohol deprivation effect, with significantly increased intake of 5% and 20% ethanol and a near-significant increase for 10%, leading to a robust rise in total ethanol consumption from baseline (~3.43 g/kg/day) to post-deprivation (~4.66 g/kg/day). The paper references prior work showing psilocybin and LY379268 reduce the ADE.
outcomes.statistics: 5%: p = 0.006; 10%: p = 0.11; 20%: p = 0.034; Total: p < 0.001 (two-sided paired t-tests).
outcomes.evidence: Following deprivation, animals displayed increased consumption of all alcohol concentrations compared to baseline drinking (5%: 1.58 ± 0.60, p = 0.006; 10%: 1.49 ± 0.47, p = 0.11; 20%: 1.59 ± 0.58, p = 0.034, Total: 4.66 ± 0.64, p = < 0.001 ...) revealing a pronounced ADE.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Intake of 5%, 10%, 20% ethanol solutions, total ethanol intake, and relapse intensity (ADE-BL) are reported separately.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Daily intake values are summarised rather than analysed as within-session time-courses.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or microstructure of drinking.

B4_ethological.evidence: Voluntary home-cage drinking is a natural consummatory behaviour from the species' repertoire.

B5_social.evidence: Animals were single-housed and tested alone; no social construct measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Free-choice drinking does not require a specific cognitive task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Intake measured by bottle weighing; no automated behavioural classifier used.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only univariate comparisons and Spearman correlations are reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Rats were housed in single cages (Makrolon Type III) with bottles attached for drinking.

E2_shelter.evidence: Standard home cage with bedding and nest material; no enclosed refuge described.

E3_bedding.evidence: Rats were housed ... on sawdust bedding (Ssniff - Bedding 3/4 S, Altrogge).

E5_enrichment.evidence: No tunnels, chew toys, or other enrichment objects are mentioned.

E6_spatial.evidence: Home cage is a single compartment.

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were housed in single cages; no conspecific present during drinking measurement.

E8_food_water.evidence: Pelleted food and water (plus ethanol bottles) were available ad libitum in the cage.

D1_continuity.evidence: Animals had continuous home-cage access to bottles; intake was monitored 24 h/day across drinking cycles over more than a year.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Drinking is recorded continuously in the home cage (24-hour access), well beyond 6 h.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Eight weeks of continuous drinking followed by multiple 4-6 week drinking phases over more than a year, with daily intake measurements.

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline consumption during the last week of a drinking phase was recorded prior to deprivation and any pharmacological intervention.

D5_followup.evidence: Intake measured on the first day after 2-3 week deprivation periods (well beyond 24 h post-dose).

D6_circadian.evidence: Home-cage drinking is monitored continuously across full day/night cycles.

assays.assay_name: Auditory oddball ERP/ERO recording with resting-state ECoG
assays.assay_description: Awake rats placed in a rodent sling within a sound-insulated audiometry booth while prefrontal epidural ECoG was recorded. A two-tone auditory oddball paradigm (standards 1 kHz/70 dB 87%, deviants 2 kHz/80 dB 13%; 1620 tones in 6 blocks of 5 min) elicited ERPs (P1, N1, P2, N2, P3 components and peak-to-peak amplitudes) and event-related oscillations (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma). Additional 5-min resting-state recordings were obtained immediately before and ~1 h after acute i.p. psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg) or LY379268 (1 mg/kg). The recorded behavioural output is the animal's stimulus-locked sensory/cognitive response; data analysed are electrophysiological.

application_type.evidence: alcohol-dependent rats randomly received intraperitoneal (i.p.) injections of psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg) ... or LY379268 (1 mg/kg) ... each 30 min before recording.

setup_habituation.evidence: During the final two-week period of alcohol deprivation, the animals were habituated to the recording set-up and underwent surgery to implant the neuroprosthetic device.

setup_restrain.evidence: One animal at a time was placed in a rodent sling (Lomir Biomedical Inc.) to reduce movement artefacts within an electrically shielded and sound-insulated audiometry booth.

food_restriction.evidence: Recording took place in an audiometry booth with the rat in a sling; no food bowl was present during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Recording took place in an audiometry booth with the rat in a sling; no water bottle was available during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg) ... or LY379268 (1 mg/kg) ... each 30 min before recording.

sample_size.evidence: Graphs illustrated in black: alcohol- and drug-naive controls (n = 10), red: alcohol-dependent animals (n = 10), green: alcohol-dependent animals that received a single dose of psilocybin, blue: alcohol-dependent animals that received a single dose of LY379268.

outcomes.summary: Although the primary readouts are electrophysiological (ERP/ERO/PSD), the behavioural paradigm itself is the auditory oddball task. Alcohol-dependent rats showed reduced P1N1/N1P2 amplitudes, attenuated delta/theta/alpha/beta ERO power and high-beta-dominant resting state compared to naive controls. Acute psilocybin and LY379268 restored P1N1 and N1P2 amplitudes, shifted maximum beta power to lower frequencies and reduced resting-state power across bands.
outcomes.statistics: rmANOVA with treatment and channel factors and Sidak-adjusted multiple comparisons; significant effects reported as *p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001 (detailed F/p values in Tables S1, S4, S7, S11, S14).
outcomes.evidence: Acute application of psilocybin and LY379268 increased amplitudes of P1N1 and N1P2 components in our alcohol-dependent rats and ... elevated bandpowers over the entire frequency range. ... both pharmacotreatments shifted maximum beta powers from mid/high beta ranges to lower frequencies.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Reported measures include P1N1, N1P2, P2N2, N2P3 amplitudes; P1/N1/P2/N2/P3 latencies; delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma ERO power; latencies and frequencies of maximum ERO power; and resting-state PSD per band.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: ERP and ERO analyses examine stimulus-locked changes over time within the post-stimulus window (e.g. P1 20-70 ms, P3 130-600 ms), and time-frequency ERSP traces show within-session temporal dynamics.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions or sequences is reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: The task measures stimulus-evoked neuroelectric responses during passive listening, not naturalistic behaviours.

B5_social.evidence: Single animal in a sound-insulated booth; no social component.

B6_cognitive.evidence: The auditory oddball paradigm relies on detection of infrequent deviant tones, engaging selective attention and executive control.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Signal processing used EEGLAB filtering, epoching and spectral analysis; no pose estimation or behavioural ML classifier.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Statistical analyses are rmANOVAs and Spearman correlations on individual measures; no PCA/UMAP/cluster analyses.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Recording took place in a sound-insulated audiometry booth with the rat in a rodent sling.

E2_shelter.evidence: Animal is restrained in a sling within an open booth; no shelter.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the recording apparatus (rodent sling in audiometry booth).

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the recording apparatus.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects in the recording apparatus.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single-compartment audiometry booth with the animal restrained in a sling.

E7_social_context.evidence: One animal at a time was placed in a rodent sling.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water provided in the audiometry booth during recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: ECoG recordings were performed three days post-surgery (no drug) and on days 6 and 9 post-surgery with psilocybin or LY379268.

D2_session_duration.evidence: The auditory oddball paradigm consisted of altogether 1620 tones ... delivered in 6 × 5 min blocks plus short breaks, with additional 5-min pre- and post-drug resting-state recordings, giving a total session of ~30-40 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Recordings on day 3 (baseline), day 6 and day 9 post-surgery (psilocybin or LY379268 in randomized order) = 3 recording days for this assay.

D4_baseline.evidence: ECoG recordings without any further interventions were implemented three days after the animals had undergone surgery ... The initial recording measured a state of abstinence in alcohol-dependent rats compared to matched alcohol-naïve rats.

D5_followup.evidence: Recordings were performed 30 min after acute injection; no recordings ≥24 h after drug administration are reported.

D6_circadian.evidence: Sessions are ~30-40 min, well below 6 h.

judge_notes: Included two assays: (1) the long-term voluntary alcohol drinking / ADE paradigm (a behavioural paradigm whose primary outcome — ethanol intake — is reported and statistically analysed here), and (2) the auditory oddball paradigm during which ECoG was recorded. The oddball is a behavioural paradigm (selective attention to deviant tones) even though the readouts are electrophysiological; scored per rubric guidance that behavioural tasks combined with neural recording should be scored on the behavioural component.
Excluded pure electrophysiology/biomarker analyses (resting-state ECoG, ERPs, EROs) as standalone assays — they are recording modalities within the oddball assay.
Total n_male set to 20 (10 alcohol-dependent + 10 naive controls); candidate gptoss reported only the dependent cohort.
Vehicle for psilocybin set to 'water' (Ampuwa = sterile water for injection).
Housing enrichment marked 'yes' based on explicit mention of Bed-r' Nest material in home cage.
Setup restraint scored 'yes' for the ECoG/oddball assay because animals were placed in a rodent sling during recording, which constitutes body restraint (distinct from injection restraint).
